extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys/agents), USPTO OED staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural rules, and sanctions governing disciplinary proceedings against practitioners before the USPTO, including what conduct violates the Code of Professional Responsibility and the range of remedies (reprimand, probation, suspension) and notice/publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters under 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings against registered practitioners are brought under these statutes/regulations; settlement agreements and Final Orders are processed and approved pursuant to these authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Part 10 Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent practitioners are subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth in Part 10 of Title 37, Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners' conduct before the Office is evaluated under Part 10 standards (e.g., §§10.23, 10.77).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must be paid in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees and charges payable to the USPTO are required to be paid in advance; that is, at the time of requesting any action by the USPTO for which a fee or charge is payable (37 C.F.R. § 1.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay required fees at the time of requesting action can result in the Office not taking the requested action (e.g., not reviving an application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted payment methods for patent processing fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application processing fees may be paid by check, cashier's check, money order, credit card, or via authorization to charge a deposit account if one is established (37 C.F.R. §§ 1.23 and 1.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of appropriate and viable payment mechanisms is required; submitting checks that are dishonored can have professional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of filing date without basic filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 1.53, an application for a patent may be assigned a filing date without payment of the basic filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a narrow exception to the advance-payment rule; other fees remain subject to § 1.22 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that reflects adversely on a practitioner's fitness to practice is proscribed; submitting checks drawn on accounts with insufficient funds was found to violate § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing/submitting dishonored checks to the USPTO (even if to cover client fees) can constitute conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice and support discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of a legal matter (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to take appropriate action on a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner (e.g., failing to revive unintentionally abandoned patent applications) violates § 10.77(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect includes omissions that result in clients' applications not being revived; such neglect may be the basis for disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand and probation as sanction options
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose a public reprimand and a probationary period (example here: public reprimand plus 24-month probation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreed sanctions in a settlement can include public reprimand and specified probation durations; the practitioner may continue to practice during probation unless suspended later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement and Order to Show Cause procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the practitioner's address of record, and grant fifteen days to respond; the OED Director may then forward the matter to the USPTO Director requesting suspension up to 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets forth notice, response period, and escalation procedures for alleged probation violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension effects and administrative steps upon suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended, the OED Director shall disseminate information per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; the USPTO will dissociate the practitioner's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; the practitioner may not apply for or obtain a Customer Number or PKI certificate until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension triggers dissociation from electronic credentials and public notice; reinstatement prerequisites apply before regaining access.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic stay of suspension during review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director enters an order suspending the practitioner and the practitioner seeks review, such review shall not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance the USPTO Director's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner cannot delay the effect of suspension by seeking review; suspension takes immediate effect as ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and shall publish a notice materially consistent with the Final Order in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary outcomes are publicly posted and summarized; Official Gazette notices provide a public statement of discipline and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State bars and courts are notified of USPTO discipline as part of inter-agency communication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may pursue additional discipline under §§ 11.34–11.57
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in a settlement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline against the practitioner under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for misconduct that caused a suspension under the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement or sanction here does not waive the Office's authority to initiate further disciplinary proceedings under the broader enforcement regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigating circumstances (e.g., health issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical or health problems that adversely affected a practitioner's ability to represent clients can be acknowledged by the practitioner and may be presented as mitigating information in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of treatment and readiness to resume competent practice may be considered in determining discipline, but does not preclude finding violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner's obligation to repay outstanding USPTO fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner remains obligated to pay any outstanding USPTO fees associated with client matters and should take steps to pay amounts due (examples: owing $160 and $200 in cited matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repayment of outstanding fees is recognized and the practitioner may acknowledge and take steps to satisfy obligations; failure to pay can be relevant to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record may be used in future disciplinary proceedings or as aggravating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents the Office from considering the record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, in addressing further complaints or in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior discipline can be used to increase sanctions in later proceedings or to counter respondent's representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client notification under 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the practitioner discussed with clients the status of their patent applications and appropriate action, notification under 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4) may not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order noted that because the respondent represented that he had discussed matters with his clients, an additional notification requirement was not invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreements and allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent may enter a settlement agreement resolving disciplinary action which, when approved, becomes a Final Order; parties may agree that each bears their own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlements can resolve pending complaints and specify sanctions/cost allocation; final approval is by the Under Secretary/USPTO Director.
